clue.text: Overhasty, forward missing header

indicators.note: missing its header means the word loses its first letter, the one at the top of this down entry

parts.note: brash means forward or cheekily bold

explanation.surface: Someone criticised as overhasty and too forward, lacking a proper headline or lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is one taken too hastily, without thought, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Wealthy heiress in car, on the phone

indicators.note: words heard on the phone are only heard, so the clue gives a word by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a Porsche is a make of sports car

explanation.surface: A rich young heiress chatting on her phone while sitting in her car.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech PORSCHE is said 'POR-sha', the same as the name PORTIA; 'in' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the rich heiress of Belmont courted by suitors in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Likely to happen, being terribly honest about character

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed letters go round the other piece
terribly suggests the letters are badly treated and knocked out of order

parts.note: a card is a character, an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A prediction that someone's very honest nature is about to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like moral fibre to go with 'honest', but here it is a card, an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the cards is a likely prospect, an idiom from fortune-telling with playing cards.

clue.text: Injured party starts to video it, Chelsea tractor in motion

indicators.note: starts to these words means take the opening letter of each word in turn

explanation.surface: Someone hurt by a big off-road car in Chelsea starts filming it as it moves.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Chelsea tractor' is British slang for a large 4x4 driven in wealthy city areas; here every word from 'video' to 'motion' gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is the person harmed or wronged, the injured party in law or in an accident.

clue.text: Traitor shot, on film

parts.note: a shot is a go or attempt, also called a turn
a film is a thin layer, a coat of something

explanation.surface: A traitor is shot dead, and the execution is captured on film.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts their side for the opposition, a synonym for a traitor.

clue.text: More than one bar is to be found round centre of Pinner

indicators.note: round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a six-letter word is its two middle letters

parts.note: the middle two letters of Pinner

explanation.surface: Several pubs can be found around the middle of Pinner, a suburb in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are pubs, and a bar is a pub, so more than one bar gives the plural.

clue.text: Gripping, a trial broadcast involving leader of Democrats

indicators.note: involving means the first piece takes in the other piece
broadcast means spoken out over the air, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Democrats

explanation.surface: A gripping televised court case featuring the head of the Democratic party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns HEARING into its sound-alike HERING; A + HERING then has the D from 'leader of Democrats' slipped in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhering means sticking fast to something, so it is a synonym for gripping in the sense of holding on.

clue.text: Rolling with laughter at home, son held up by very small people

indicators.note: held up by in a down clue means sitting on top of the following piece

parts.note: at home means in
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
titch is British slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: Someone laughing at home after their son is supported by tiny children.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is informal British for a very small person, often a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in stitches is an idiom for laughing uncontrollably, like rolling about with mirth.

clue.text: A cereal, and fruit

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A breakfast pairing: a bowl of cereal and some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit' looks like part of the breakfast list, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, and botanically a nut is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Massive dinosaur droppings gathered by one college fellow

indicators.note: gathered by means collected up by, so one comes first and takes the droppings after it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats
a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.surface: An Oxford academic collects fossilised dung from a huge dinosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous, among the first identified.

clue.text: Bigwig in recently taken photo

parts.note: hot means fresh or just made, as in hot off the press
a shot is a photograph

explanation.surface: A self-important bigwig appears in a newly snapped picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is an important or highly successful person, much like a bigwig.

clue.text: There's nothing to get worked up about on waste ground

definitions.text: There's nothing to get worked up about

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone says a patch of waste ground is no cause for fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun after 'waste', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no sweat' is a casual way of saying a task is easy and nothing to fret about.

clue.text: Pope is missing money in Zurich?

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: Francis was the name of the recent Pope

explanation.surface: The Pope has lost his wallet while visiting Zurich.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss franc is the currency used in Zurich; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Fine Italian police series suited one's needs

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth
The Bill was a long-running British TV police drama

explanation.surface: An Italian police drama that was just what viewers wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bill is also British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit the bill is an idiom meaning to be exactly what is required.

clue.text: Low temperature affected Pinot? Bone of contention

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Wine buffs argue over whether chilling spoiled a Pinot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like it describes the temperature, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is an issue open to debate, which is what a bone of contention is.

clue.text: Fine spring? Mostly

parts.note: pretty means fine or attractive
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Asked if spring has been fine, someone answers that it mostly has.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty well means almost entirely or largely, synonymous with mostly.

clue.text: Very reliable person's powerful tractor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dependable, supportive person; the 's is read as 'is'
second meaning, punning: a strong thing that tows, a tower full of strength

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits TOWER as 'one who tows', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for a person who gives steadfast support in hard times.

clue.text: Turn on wench providing winch

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle
a wench is an old word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: Someone turns to a serving girl, provided she brings a lifting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a hand-cranked drum for hauling rope, a kind of winch.

clue.text: Takes in better size of paper

parts.note: to take in is to deceive or fool
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a larger sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a traditional British paper format, slightly longer than A4.

clue.text: Workers getting beaten comprehensively

parts.note: hands are labourers or workers
down means defeated or beaten

explanation.surface: The labour force is soundly thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning hands down means winning easily and decisively, so the phrase means utterly or comprehensively.

clue.text: Refinement seen in Venice, typically

indicators.note: seen in means the letters can be spotted spanning these words

explanation.surface: A typical Venetian elegance, perhaps in its architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or subtle distinction, a refinement of manners or precision.

clue.text: Charge cut by smallholder, initially, for bundle of straw?

indicators.note: cut means the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: a trust is a charge, something given into one's care

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of smallholder

explanation.surface: A farmer with a small plot is charged for a bale of straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks TRUST to TRUS; 'by' then just sets S beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a bundle of hay or straw tied up; the question mark admits it may be hay instead.

clue.text: Defend winning wrestling move

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up
a hold is a grip used in wrestling

explanation.surface: A wrestler defends a title with a winning move.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold is to support or maintain, as in defending a decision or principle.

clue.text: Roars from the Spanish fans outside

indicators.note: outside means the first piece sits around the second

parts.note: to fan air is to blow it
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish football fans roaring at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like supporters, but it is the verb meaning blows.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to shout loudly, so bellows is a synonym for roars.

clue.text: Local line running through Rochester

indicators.note: running through means the letters lie within the word

explanation.surface: A local railway line runs through Rochester, a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British for the neighbourhood pub, where darts is played.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line a darts player stands behind when throwing, found in a pub.

clue.text: Hit hard on the head protecting wife in farm building

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: to cosh is to strike with a heavy club, usually on the head

explanation.surface: A violent attack in a barn while protecting a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is a farm outbuilding for housing cattle.

clue.text: Remove weed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cut off or deduct

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to a gardener; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dock means to cut short or deduct, and is also the common name of the Rumex plant.

clue.text: Become disillusioned let ashore abroad

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor allowed off ship in a foreign land grows disillusioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become discouraged and give up hope.

clue.text: I put in call about flower

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other piece
about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone phones a florist about ordering a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CALL to LLAC, and 'put in' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white blossoms.
